title: A Population Slowdown in the U.S.

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 甚至在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ时，你每晚都要带上300张最珍贵的唱片去工作，你会把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成一个类似充满美感的50年前老物件的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 这里是《纽约我是》时报，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: A few days ago, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 几天前，美国

sentences.en: government revealed that the country's population is growing at the slowest rate in nearly a century.
sentences.zh: 政府透露，该国人口增长率正处于近一个世纪以来的最低水平。

sentences.en: Today, Asted Herndon spoke with our colleague,
sentences.zh: 今天，阿斯特德·赫恩登与我们的同事

sentences.en: Sabrina Tavernisi, about why that is and just how profoundly it could shape America's future.
sentences.zh: 萨布丽娜·塔韦内齐一起探讨了背后的原因，以及这可能对美国未来产生的深远影响。

sentences.en: Tuesday, May 4th.
sentences.zh: 5月4日，星期二。

sentences.en: So, Sabrina, when the U.S.
sentences.zh: 萨布丽娜，当美国

sentences.en: government finished counting the American people this time in the census, it found that the American population was growing really slowly.
sentences.zh: 政府在这次人口普查中完成对美国人口的统计时，他们发现美国人口增长非常缓慢。

sentences.en: That was a bit surprising to me, personally.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，这有点出乎意料。

sentences.en: What's going on here?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: So, this is a very interesting and relatively new thing for the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以，对美国来说，这是一个非常有趣且相对较新的现象。

sentences.en: We have this extremely slow population increase, which is different for the United States.
sentences.zh: 我们的这种人口增长极为缓慢，这与美国以往的情况不同。

sentences.en: The United States usually grows really quickly.
sentences.zh: 美国通常增长得非常快。

sentences.en: What we saw with the census data was the second slowest decade for population growth in American history.
sentences.zh: 我们在普查数据中看到的是美国历史上人口增长第二慢的十年。

sentences.en: That is, since 1790, when the United States government started taking the census.
sentences.zh: 也就是自1790年美国政府开始进行人口普查以来。

sentences.en: So, that's really surprising.
sentences.zh: 所以，这真的很让人意外。

sentences.en: We had known that there was some slowdown for some time, but this census data really tells us this is really the new normal in the United States.
sentences.zh: 我们一段时间以来就知道人口增长有所放缓，但这次的人口普查数据明确告诉我们，这确实成了美国的新常态。

sentences.en: So, population is growing at a slower rate.
sentences.zh: 因此，人口增长率正在放缓。

sentences.en: How do we explain this?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何解释这一点？

sentences.en: So, Estad, there are two forces that make up population growth.
sentences.zh: 阿斯特德，构成人口增长的动力主要有两个。

sentences.en: One is immigration, and the other is births.
sentences.zh: 一个是移民，另一个是出生人口。

sentences.en: Then, of course, there are deaths.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有死亡人口。

sentences.en: So, you put all of these things together, and that's what makes a population grow.
sentences.zh: 所以，把所有这些因素结合在一起，就是人口增长的原因。

sentences.en: And so, for the past decade or so, we've seen a real slowdown in immigration.
sentences.zh: 因此，在过去的十年左右里，我们看到移民数量明显放缓。

sentences.en: And there are a number of reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 这背后有诸多原因。

sentences.en: A lot fewer people coming from Mexico.
sentences.zh: 来自墨西哥的人数大幅减少。

sentences.en: That's in part because the Mexican economy is a bit better.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是墨西哥经济有所好转。

sentences.en: The birth rate in Mexico itself has gone way down, so there's less pressure for people to come to the United States to work.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥本土的出生率已经大幅下降，因此人们来美国工作的压力变小了。

sentences.en: But the real interesting part of what's going on and the real mystery is the birth rate.
sentences.zh: 但最有趣、最让人费解的部分其实是出生率。

sentences.en: So, the birth rate began to decline in 2008 during the financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 出生率是在2008年金融危机期间开始下降的。

sentences.en: And we would expect that because birth rates tend to decline when countries have financial crises, when they're in economic distress.
sentences.zh: 这是我们可以预料的，因为当国家遭遇金融危机或经济困境时，出生率往往会下降。

sentences.en: People put off having babies.
sentences.zh: 人们会推迟要孩子的时间。

sentences.en: But usually, once the economy starts to pick up again, the birth rate goes back up.
sentences.zh: 但通常情况下，一旦经济开始回暖，出生率就会回升。

sentences.en: And that's precisely what demographers were expecting to happen in 2009, 10, and 11.
sentences.zh: 这正是人口学家预计在2009、2010和2011年发生的事情。

sentences.en: But something very strange happened.
sentences.zh: 但发生了一件非常奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: Which was the birth rate kept going down.
sentences.zh: 那就是出生率一直在持续下降。

sentences.en: It went down and down and down.
sentences.zh: 它一路下跌，不断刷新低谷。

sentences.en: And no one could understand why.
sentences.zh: 没有人能理解这是为什么。

sentences.en: So, it used to be that there were 2.1 children born to every American woman.
sentences.zh: 过去，平均每个美国女性会生育2.1个孩子。

sentences.en: That was before 2008.
sentences.zh: 那是2008年之前的事了。

sentences.en: That's exactly enough to replace their parents when they die.
sentences.zh: 这刚好足够在父母去世时进行人口更替。

sentences.en: That's called replacement-level fertility.
sentences.zh: 这被称为更替水平生育率。

sentences.en: But now it's 1.7 children per woman, which is below the rate of replacement.
sentences.zh: 但现在每位女性只有1.7个孩子，低于更替水平。

sentences.en: So, if we didn't have any immigration at all, our population would actually be declining.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们完全没有移民，我们的人口实际上会不断减少。

sentences.en: Eventually, yes.
sentences.zh: 最终是的。

sentences.en: And that has opened up this whole new line of inquiry.
sentences.zh: 这也开启了一个全新的研究方向。

sentences.en: Demographers are asking, why is this happening?
sentences.zh: 人口学家们都在追问：为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Well, let's get into those ideas.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们深入探讨这些观点。

sentences.en: Why do folks think, why do demographers, economists think, that the birth rate is declining?
sentences.zh: 为什么大家、为什么人口学家和经济学家认为出生率在下降？

sentences.en: So, the most straightforward theory right now is that it's about the economy.
sentences.zh: 目前最直接的理论是这与经济有关。

sentences.en: So, essentially, you have this large group of American women, younger millennials, women in their 20s, who are putting off having children.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，这庞大的一群美国女性——年轻的千禧一代、20多岁的女性——正在推迟生育。

sentences.en: And it's not because they don't want to have kids.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为她们不想生孩子。

sentences.en: They do want to have kids.
sentences.zh: 她们其实是想生孩子的。

sentences.en: We know that from survey work that's been done.
sentences.zh: 我们从已经开展的各项调查中得知这一点。

sentences.en: But they just don't feel like they can afford to have kids.
sentences.zh: 但她们只是觉得无力承担养育孩子的开销。

sentences.en: And if you think about it, this group of women, they're graduating and going out into the world as adults into a really different economy than their parents did.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细想想，这群女性大学毕业作为成年人步入社会时，面对的经济环境与她们的父母大不相同。

sentences.en: So, they have huge amounts of student debt.
sentences.zh: 她们背负着巨额的学生债务。

sentences.en: That wasn't the case in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 过去可不是这样的。

sentences.en: Home prices and rents are just skyrocketing.
sentences.zh: 房价和租金正在急剧飙升。

sentences.en: That's also very different than what their parents had.
sentences.zh: 这也与她们父母当年的情况大相径庭。

sentences.en: And there's also been 40 years of economic inequality in this country.
sentences.zh: 此外，这个国家还经历了40年的经济不平等。

sentences.en: And that has essentially made a very, very difficult job market and life for people in the lower middle classes who are trying to make it on, you know, essentially low-wage work,
sentences.zh: 这实际上让下中产阶层的人们在试图依靠（你知道的）基本上是低薪的工作来维持生计、

sentences.en: cobbling together a couple of different jobs.
sentences.zh: 同时拼凑几份不同的工作时，面临着极其艰难的就业市场和生活。

sentences.en: Schedules are incredibly erratic, which makes it very difficult to plan around a daycare pickup, right?
sentences.zh: 工作时间极其不规律，这使得人们很难围绕接送孩子去托儿所的时间做出规划，对吧？

sentences.en: And the other driver is that there's a very weak social safety net in the United States.
sentences.zh: 另一个驱动因素是美国的社会保障网非常薄弱。

sentences.en: Unlike other countries, it has a lot of holes.
sentences.zh: 与其他国家不同，它存在很多漏洞。

sentences.en: So, think about it.
sentences.zh: 试想一下。

sentences.en: No parental leave.
sentences.zh: 没有产假。

sentences.en: No sick leave.
sentences.zh: 没有病假。

sentences.en: Extremely difficult to get a childcare subsidy.
sentences.zh: 极难获得育儿补贴。

sentences.en: So, essentially what you have is this whole group of young women
sentences.zh: 所以，你基本上会看到这样一群年轻女性

sentences.en: looking out there into the economy, looking at their lives, and essentially saying, no way can I afford to have a kid right now.
sentences.zh: 放眼经济形势，审视自己的生活，然后异口同声地说：我绝对负担不起现在生孩子。

sentences.en: It's too expensive.
sentences.zh: 太贵了。

sentences.en: I can't afford it.
sentences.zh: 我养不起。

sentences.en: So, you're describing young women waiting.
sentences.zh: 所以你描述的是年轻女性在观望。

sentences.en: But when they do decide to have children eventually, are they still having the same number of children that they would have had before or not?
sentences.zh: 但当她们最终决定要孩子时，她们生育的数量还会和以前一样多吗？

sentences.en: So, the short answer is, it's really too early to tell.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答是，现在下定论还为时过早。

sentences.en: We know that when women do delay having kids, they tend to have fewer kids because they start later.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，当女性推迟生育时，由于开始得晚，她们往往会生得更少。

sentences.en: We do also know that older millennials have been having kids.
sentences.zh: 我们也确实知道，较年长的千禧一代一直在生孩子。

sentences.en: It has not been them foregoing having children altogether.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说她们彻底放弃了生育。

sentences.en: But we really don't know what will happen with the big bulk of this generation, whether this is a delay or foregoing altogether.
sentences.zh: 但我们真的不知道这代人的绝大多数最终会怎样，这究竟只是推迟还是彻底放弃。

sentences.en: Okay, so what's going on with millennials then does not seem to explain the entirety of this trend.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那么千禧一代身上发生的事情似乎并不能完全解释这一趋势。

sentences.en: No, it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 不，确实不能。

sentences.en: But there is this other theory that goes beyond economics.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一个超越经济学范畴的理论。

sentences.en: If you look at the data, you see that the absolute biggest decline has been among teens, ages 15 to 19.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看数据，就会发现绝对降幅最大的是15到19岁的青少年群体。

sentences.en: It's declined by around 80% over the past 20 years.
sentences.zh: 在过去的20年里，这一比例下降了约80%。

sentences.en: And that's really interesting, right?
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣，对吧？

sentences.en: Because those are people who really aren't quite yet in the labor force.
sentences.zh: 因为这些人实际上还没有真正进入劳动力市场。

sentences.en: So, what is motivating them?
sentences.zh: 那么是什么在激励他们呢？

sentences.en: Why have teenagers practically stopped having pregnancies?
sentences.zh: 为什么青少年的怀孕率几乎停滞了？

sentences.en: That's a really big change.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常巨大的变化。

sentences.en: And so, when we look at that, what we see is a couple of reasons.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们审视这一点时，我们看到了几个原因。

sentences.en: Again, these are theories.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，这些都还只是理论。

sentences.en: One is that contraception use has gone up.
sentences.zh: 其一是避孕措施的使用率有所上升。

sentences.en: So, that's a behavioral change for teens.
sentences.zh: 所以这是青少年行为上的一种改变。

sentences.en: That didn't used to be the case in the 1980s, 1990s.
sentences.zh: 这在20世纪80和90年代并不是这样的。

sentences.en: Another is that teenagers are actually having sex less.
sentences.zh: 另一个原因是青少年的性行为确实减少了。

sentences.en: There's a whole kind of new area of thinking and research and work about, you know, how social media has changed us, how smartphones have changed us.
sentences.zh: 关于社交媒体如何改变了我们、智能手机如何改变了我们，有一整套崭新的思考、研究和工作领域。

sentences.en: Kids are spending more time online.
sentences.zh: 孩子们花在网上的时间更多了。

sentences.en: There's pornography people are using.
sentences.zh: 人们在观看色情内容。

sentences.en: They have much easier access to.
sentences.zh: 他们获取这些内容的途径要容易得多。

sentences.en: And then another idea about this very young group is that perhaps there's something good going on for them about the American economy and the way they see their futures.
sentences.zh: 关于这个非常年轻的群体，还有另一种观点，即美国经济以及他们对未来的看法可能对他们产生了一些积极的影响。

sentences.en: That these young women feel like there's a real reason to hold off having children because there's a real chance for them to make it, to go to community college,
sentences.zh: 这些年轻女性觉得有充分的理由推迟生育，因为她们有真正的机会去获得成功、去读社区学院、

sentences.en: to come out in a place where it makes sense to not have their baby until they're 28 or 29 instead of 21 and 22, which it had always been.
sentences.zh: 在28或29岁而不是像以往那样的21或22岁生孩子，这在当时显得更为合理。

sentences.en: So these are obviously really good things, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这些显然都是非常好的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Public health officials spent decades trying to convince young women not to have babies in their teens.
sentences.zh: 公共卫生官员花了几十年时间试图说服年轻女性不要在十几岁时生孩子。

sentences.en: You know, teen pregnancy was a whole public health problem that people were trying to solve.
sentences.zh: 你知道，青少年怀孕曾是一个人们极力想要解决的公共卫生难题。

sentences.en: And they essentially solved it.
sentences.zh: 而他们基本上把它解决了。

sentences.en: I mean, it's for all intents and purposes,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从所有实际意图和目的来看，

sentences.en: dramatically declined.
sentences.zh: 它已经急剧下降。

sentences.en: And women are taking more control over their lives and over childbearing.
sentences.zh: 女性正在对自己的生活和生育拥有更多的控制权。

sentences.en: And when you look at the rates of unintended pregnancy, those are down really dramatically.
sentences.zh: 当你查看意外怀孕的比率时，它们确实大幅下降了。

sentences.en: So that gives us another clue as to what's going on here, that there's some behavioral change as well as the economics.
sentences.zh: 这为我们提供了另一个线索，让我们了解这里发生了什么：除了经济因素之外，还存在一些行为上的改变。

sentences.en: There's something else going on.
sentences.zh: 还有其他事情正在发生。

sentences.en: Okay, so you're describing changes that happen among millennial women and also women who are younger than millennials.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你描述的是千禧一代女性以及比千禧一代更年轻的女性身上发生的变化。

sentences.en: So that spans from teenagers all the way through women in their 30s.
sentences.zh: 所以这涵盖了从青少年一直到30多岁的女性。

sentences.en: But I'm also interested in a different slice of that population, immigrants.
sentences.zh: 但我对这一人群中的另一个细分群体——移民，也同样感兴趣。

sentences.en: Are birth rates declining among that population as well?
sentences.zh: 那个群体的出生率也在下降吗？

sentences.en: So, Ested, this is very interesting because, in fact, the birth rate is declining most precipitously among precisely that group.
sentences.zh: 阿斯特德，这非常有趣，因为事实上，出生率下降最急剧的恰恰是这个群体。

sentences.en: So for a long time, the kind of story about what was going on was that immigrants who were coming in were having many more children.
sentences.zh: 所以在很长一段时间里，关于所发生事情的一种说法是，新来的移民会生更多的孩子。

sentences.en: And to a certain extent, that was true.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这确实是真的。

sentences.en: Women who were coming from Mexico in the 1980s and 1990s, and even in the early 2000s, they were coming from families where there were six and seven children in the family.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪80年代、90年代甚至2000年代初来到美国的墨西哥女性，她们来自拥有六、七个孩子的家庭。

sentences.en: And they were arriving to the United States and they were having more babies and having babies younger.
sentences.zh: 她们来到美国后生了更多孩子，并且生育年龄更早。

sentences.en: So this was really kind of boosting the birth rate a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实在很大程度上推动了出生率的上升。

sentences.en: But what happened was their children changed.
sentences.zh: 但后来发生的事情是，她们的孩子变了。

sentences.en: Their children were born in the United States and they acted a lot more like everyone else who was born in the United States, which meant they had far fewer children and later.
sentences.zh: 她们的孩子出生在美国，行事风格越来越像在美国出生的其他人，这意味着他们生育的孩子要少得多，而且生得更晚。

sentences.en: So this is a huge change from the immigrant generation to their native-born children.
sentences.zh: 因此，从移民一代到在当地出生的子女，这是一个巨大的转变。

sentences.en: Okay, so many women are delaying childbirth as an economic calculation or as just a general life calculation.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以很多女性推迟生育是出于经济考量，或者只是一种普遍的人生规划。

sentences.en: That seems to make total sense.
sentences.zh: 这听起来完全合乎情理。

sentences.en: It does seem to make sense.
sentences.zh: 这确实说得通。

sentences.en: But here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 但问题是这样的。

sentences.en: When you zoom out and compare the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当你把视角拉远，将美国

sentences.en: to other developed countries, it actually gets a lot more confusing because actually this is starting to happen in all rich countries around the world.
sentences.zh: 与其他发达国家进行比较时，情况实际上变得更加令人困惑，因为这其实开始在世界各地所有富裕国家上演。

sentences.en: Most developed countries are seeing this decline in the birth rate.
sentences.zh: 大多数发达国家都出现了出生率下降的趋势。

sentences.en: Germany, Spain, Italy, France,
sentences.zh: 德国、西班牙、意大利、法国，

sentences.en: lots of countries in Europe and also countries in East Asia,
sentences.zh: 欧洲的许多国家，还有东亚的国家，

sentences.en: South Korea, Japan.
sentences.zh: 韩国、日本。

sentences.en: And so it's very confusing because these countries have really different economies than the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常令人费解，因为这些国家的经济状况与美国截然不同。

sentences.en: And these countries have really different social safety nets.
sentences.zh: 这些国家的社会保障网也完全不同。

sentences.en: The Scandinavian countries have very strong social safety nets.
sentences.zh: 斯堪的纳维亚国家拥有非常强大的社会保障网。

sentences.en: But yet this birth rate is also dropping in these places.
sentences.zh: 然而这些地方的出生率也在下降。

sentences.en: So what is going on?
sentences.zh: 那么到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: That these countries with certainly stronger social safety nets and to some extent better economies are also experiencing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 为什么这些社会保障网无疑更强、在某种程度上经济也更好的国家，也在经历着同样的事情。

sentences.en: So one of the working hypotheses is that this fundamentally is the place where women want to be.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一个主要的假设是，从根本上说，这里正是女性想要生活的地方。

sentences.en: that they want fewer children, that they want precisely the number of children that they're actually having.
sentences.zh: 也就是她们想要更少的孩子，她们希望拥有的孩子数量恰好就是她们实际生下来的数量。

sentences.en: That as time has gone on, they've become more attached to the labor market.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，她们对劳动力市场的依赖和融合程度越来越高。

sentences.en: They've developed careers.
sentences.zh: 她们发展了自己的职业生涯。

sentences.en: They have rising pay in relation to men.
sentences.zh: 与男性相比，她们的收入在不断上涨。

sentences.en: And that means that they are wanting to have babies at times that make sense for them in the labor market.
sentences.zh: 这意味着她们希望在劳动力市场中对自己最有利的时期生育孩子。

sentences.en: So one of the arguments is that this is simply going to be the new normal for modern societies in which women are more equal with men.
sentences.zh: 因此，其中的一种观点是，对于男女更加平等的现代社会而言，这简而言之将成为一种新的常态。

sentences.en: Okay, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 好的，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: So what I am hearing is the common reporter frustration that we have a lot of theories as to why this is happening, but we don't know for sure why it's happening.
sentences.zh: 所以我听到的是记者们普遍感到的沮丧，我们有关于为什么会发生这种现象的很多理论，但我们却无法百分之百确切地知道原因。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: There's not a lot of certainty.
sentences.zh: 并没有太多的确定性。

sentences.en: Demographers will be really quick to tell you we're really just in uncharted waters right now.
sentences.zh: 人口学家会非常迅速地告诉你，我们现在确实正处于一片未知的领域。

sentences.en: We haven't seen this trend before ever in the United States, and we've only seen it in the very, very early stages in Europe and in East Asia.
sentences.zh: 我们在美国历史上从未见过这种趋势，而且我们目前也仅在欧洲和东亚看到了它非常非常初期的阶段。

sentences.en: So the question we have to ask ourselves is how worried should we be?
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须自问的问题是：我们到底该有多担心？

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报 Dealbook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th,
I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 我将在纽约市 Dealbook 峰会的现场，采访商业、政治和文化领域一些极具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance,
sentences.zh: 万斯、

sentences.en: Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zilran Mondani, and many others live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看到其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的真实对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于 11 月 18 日在 nytimes.com 上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，你可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻报道一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望大家能锁定收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Okay, Sabrina, how worried should we be about these falling birth rates?
sentences.zh: 好了，萨布丽娜，对于这些不断下降的出生率，我们到底该有多担心？

sentences.en: So, as usual, the answer is it's complicated.
sentences.zh: 所以，和往常一样，答案是：情况很复杂。

sentences.en: But the fact is a number of economists and demographers have raised some pretty troubling alarMs.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，一些经济学家和人口学家已经敲响了相当令人担忧的警钟。

sentences.en: What are those?
sentences.zh: 具体是些什么？

sentences.en: They start with what might happen with the economy.
sentences.zh: 它们首先从经济上可能发生的情况谈起。

sentences.en: So, if you have a really, really slow-growing population, that means at some point in the pretty near future, you're going to have a much smaller workforce.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果人口增长极其极其缓慢，那就意味着在不久的将来，劳动人口规模将会缩小很多。

sentences.en: And that could be potentially a real problem for economic growth.
sentences.zh: 这可能会给经济增长带来真正的问题。

sentences.en: It's harder to keep up with big, growing, booming economies like China.
sentences.zh: 要跟上中国这样庞大、不断增长且蓬勃发展的经济体将会更加困难。

sentences.en: And there are fewer workers to support older Americans who rely on
sentences.zh: 而且将会有更少的工人去支撑那些依赖

sentences.en: Social Security, on Medicare,
sentences.zh: 社会保障、医疗保险、

sentences.en: Medicaid.
sentences.zh: 医疗补助的老年美国人。

sentences.en: There are not as many workers to pay into the tax system to support this much larger population of older people.
sentences.zh: 没有足够多的劳动人口向税收系统缴税，来支撑这个规模庞大得多的老年人群体。

sentences.en: So, to think of our society as kind of a pyramid, it requires a base of people paying in for to support those at the top.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果把我们的社会想象成一个金字塔，它就需要有一个底层的人口来缴税，以支撑塔尖的人群。

sentences.en: If we don't have enough babies, if we aren't having enough young people, that pyramid gets messed up.
sentences.zh: 如果我们没有足够的婴儿，如果没有足够多的年轻人，这个金字塔就会出问题。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: Like, flip the pyramid.
sentences.zh: 比如，把金字塔倒过来。

sentences.en: So, you have this kind of tiny, spindly bottom trying to support everybody at the top, and that becomes very difficult.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，你就会发现底部变得又小又细，却试图去支撑顶部的所有人，这就会变得非常困难。

sentences.en: Americans are living much, much longer lives, and they're living at the end of their life with lots of care from caretakers who tend to be disproportionately young,
sentences.zh: 美国人的寿命变得越来越长，他们在生命最后的阶段需要大量护理人员的照顾，而这些护理人员往往年轻人偏多，

sentences.en: disproportionately female.
sentences.zh: 女性偏多。

sentences.en: That is also a concern.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个令人担忧的问题。

sentences.en: Who will take care of these people?
sentences.zh: 谁来照顾这些人？

sentences.en: Who will take care of the mostly older Americans once we get down the road into this demographic future?
sentences.zh: 当我们在未来的某一天进入这样的人口结构时，谁来照顾这些大部分是年长的美国人？

sentences.en: But the economic effects also kind of trickle down into the culture.
sentences.zh: 但经济层面的影响也会逐渐渗透到文化中。

sentences.en: So, in places that are already experiencing this in an advanced way in the United States, like a lot of counties in New England and the Plain States, some people
sentences.zh: 因此，在美国一些已经较早经历这种现象的地方，比如新英格兰和大平原地区的许多县，一些

sentences.en: living in communities like this do feel like there is a sense of kind of loss or of sadness.
sentences.zh: 生活在这样社区里的人确实感到了一种失落感或悲伤感。

sentences.en: I say this because I am from a little town in western Massachusetts that has had a lot of these same probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我这么说是因为我来自马萨诸塞州西部的一个小镇，那里也经历过许多类似的问题。

sentences.en: It's an aging population.
sentences.zh: 这是一个老龄化的人口结构。

sentences.en: My parents still live there.
sentences.zh: 我的父母仍然住在那里。

sentences.en: They're almost in their 80s.
sentences.zh: 他们快八十岁了。

sentences.en: And it's really hard to get someone to come shovel out their walk because there's not the large population of young people that there used to be.
sentences.zh: 而且很难找到人来帮他们铲雪清理人行道，因为已经没有过去那种庞大的年轻人口了。

sentences.en: My little grammar school closed,
sentences.zh: 我上的那所小型小学

sentences.en: I believe, three years ago because there just weren't enough kids to fill it.
sentences.zh: 我想大概在三年前就关门了，因为根本没有足够的小孩去填满它。

sentences.en: And I think that some people have this sense that growth means vitality, that getting bigger is good and better, and that decline is in some sense kind of signifying a death
sentences.zh: 而且我认为有些人有一种观念，认为增长就意味着活力，变大就是好事、更好，而衰退在某种意义上就象征着死亡

sentences.en: or a weakness.
sentences.zh: 或是虚弱。

sentences.en: Well, when you put it like that, I mean, both in the economic sense and in the personal senses, the schools closing, the folks without the ability to shovel out their driveways,
sentences.zh: 好吧，当你这样表述时，我是说，无论是在经济层面还是在个人层面——学校的关闭、人们无法自己清理车道——

sentences.en: it definitely feels as if this trend is a bad trend if it is one that sustains.
sentences.zh: 如果这种趋势持续下去，它确实让人觉得这是一个糟糕的趋势。

sentences.en: Are policymakers already thinking about this issue?
sentences.zh: 政策制定者已经在思考这个问题了吗？

sentences.en: There's some thinking going on around the edges of this, but it's a very big problem, and it has implications for all parts of the economy and all parts of American society.
sentences.zh: 围绕这个问题的边缘有一些思考，但这是一个非常大的问题，它对经济的各个部分和美国社会的各个部分都有深远的影响。

sentences.en: And the real question at this point is whether policymakers are going to try to stop it or reverse it or adapt and embrace it.
sentences.zh: 而目前的真正问题在于，政策制定者是会试图阻止它、扭转它，还是去适应并接受它。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Well, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这很有意思。

sentences.en: What are the options on that front?
sentences.zh: 在这方面有哪些选择？

sentences.en: What could policymakers do to actually reverse the declining birth rates?
sentences.zh: 政策制定者可以采取什么措施来真正扭转出生率下降的趋势？

sentences.en: So there are a few things.
sentences.zh: 所以有一些方法。

sentences.en: One is, you know, we see in Russia and in Hungary populist leaders rewarding women for having more children.
sentences.zh: 首先，你知道的，我们看到在俄罗斯和匈牙利，民粹主义领导人对生育更多孩子的女性给予奖励。

sentences.en: And in some sense, you know, the fact that the United States right now is getting more serious about patching up the social safety net is some nod to the fact that, you know, yes,
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，你知道的，美国现在开始更加认真地修复社会安全网，这也是对以下事实的一种认可，即，是的，

sentences.en: women need more support.
sentences.zh: 女性需要更多的支持。

sentences.en: So you could go directly to the issue of the birth rate itself and try to make conditions more advantageous for women to have more children more often.
sentences.zh: 因此，你可以直接针对出生率本身的问题，努力为女性创造更有利的条件，让她们更频繁地生更多的孩子。

sentences.en: But the other piece of this, which we need to remember, is, of course, immigration.
sentences.zh: 但我们需要记住的另一个部分，当然就是移民。

sentences.en: That is the other big driver of population growth.
sentences.zh: 这是人口增长的另一个主要驱动力。

sentences.en: And immigration has gone down substantially over the past
sentences.zh: 在过去的十年里，移民人数大幅下降，

sentences.en: 10 years, but that is a policy decision.
sentences.zh: 但这其实是一项政策决定。

sentences.en: The government could open up immigration to many more people.
sentences.zh: 政府可以向更多的人开放移民。

sentences.en: Now, as we know in the United States, that is quite politically fraught, and that is potentially a big fight.
sentences.zh: 然而，正如我们在美国所知，这在政治上充满了争议，并可能引发一场大争论。

sentences.en: So it's not so easy as to just, you know, turn on or off a spigot.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不像打开或关闭水龙头那么简单。

sentences.en: But in terms of the economy and growth and what the future is for the population, immigration is an absolutely critical piece of that.
sentences.zh: 但就经济、增长以及人口的未来而言，移民绝对是一个至关重要的环节。

sentences.en: So those are the options to reversing the declining birth rate.
sentences.zh: 这就是扭转出生率下降的选择。

sentences.en: What are the options of adapting to that reality and basically living with an aging and changing population?
sentences.zh: 而适应这种现实并基本上与老龄化和变化的人口共存的选择又是什么呢？

sentences.en: So if the trend sticks,
sentences.zh: 如果这种趋势持续下去，

sentences.en: policymakers are going to have a lot of work to do to plan for how we care for this much larger older population.
sentences.zh: 政策制定者将有很多工作要做，来规划我们如何照顾这个庞大得多的老年人群体。

sentences.en: That inverted pyramid we talked about where we're going to have many more older people than younger people,
sentences.zh: 我们刚才谈到的那个倒金字塔，即我们将拥有比年轻人多得多的老年人，

sentences.en: that will continue to be true unless this trend reverses.
sentences.zh: 除非这种趋势扭转，否则这种情况将继续存在。

sentences.en: And that's going to be really expensive.
sentences.zh: 这将是极其昂贵的。

sentences.en: So we have to figure that out.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须弄清楚这一点。

sentences.en: We have to plan for it.
sentences.zh: 我们必须为此做好规划。

sentences.en: And it's really, really difficult.
sentences.zh: 而且这真的非常、非常困难。

sentences.en: So the other piece of this is the economy.
sentences.zh: 所以这其中的另一个部分就是经济。

sentences.en: If we choose to accept this and to adapt, that might mean accepting that we're just not going to be the major market superpower that we had been.
sentences.zh: 如果我们选择接受并适应这一点，那可能就意味着我们不得不承认，我们将不再是过去那样的主要市场超级大国。

sentences.en: And that adaptation, you know, that might be hard to swallow.
sentences.zh: 而这种适应，你知道的，可能有点难以接受。

sentences.en: America's superpower status and supereconomic status is pretty fundamental to how the country sees itself in the global stage.
sentences.zh: 美国的超级大国地位和超级经济地位，对于这个国家如何在国际舞台上看待自己至关重要。

sentences.en: Both these options seem pretty fraught then.
sentences.zh: 那么，这两种选择看起来都充满了争议。

sentences.en: I mean, what you're explaining for either incentivizing new births or in terms of adapting to a declining birth rate, both those options seem like they require a real societal
sentences.zh: 我是说，你刚才解释的无论是激励新生儿还是适应出生率下降的方案，这两种选择似乎都需要对社会进行真正的

sentences.en: restructuring.
sentences.zh: 重组。

sentences.en: Those are big things.
sentences.zh: 这些都是大事。

sentences.en: So how do we decide which one to choose?
sentences.zh: 那我们该如何决定选择哪一个呢？

sentences.en: For example, is there any reason that a declining birth rate could be a good thing and that it's actually preferable for us to continue down the road with this trend?
sentences.zh: 例如，有没有什么理由说明出生率下降可能是一件好事，而且我们实际上更愿意让这种趋势继续发展下去？

sentences.en: So first of all, it could be good for the climate.
sentences.zh: 所以首先，这对气候可能有好处。

sentences.en: Climate change is happening all around us and a smaller population could be a more sustainable way to live on the earth and that is something that people are talking about a lot.
sentences.zh: 气候变化就在我们身边发生，较少的人口可能是地球上更具可持续性的生活方式，这是人们经常讨论的话题。

sentences.en: Also, in the economy, a slightly smaller population of workers would give workers themselves more clout and more ability to bargain, to have higher wages.
sentences.zh: 此外，在经济方面，略微减少的劳动人口会赋予工人本身更大的话语权和议价能力，从而获得更高的工资。

sentences.en: Another example is for the next generation of children, fewer children and families could lead to more investment in each individual child.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子是对于下一代儿童而言，更少的孩子和家庭可以带来对每个孩子更多的投资。

sentences.en: More likely that that child will be able to go to college, more tutoring time, more invested in each kid.
sentences.zh: 这个孩子更有可能上大学，获得更多的辅导时间，每个孩子都能获得更多的投入。

sentences.en: Sabrina, personally, I never thought much about
sentences.zh: 萨布丽娜，就我个人而言，我从来没有多想过

sentences.en: America's birth rate and I think a lot of folks are like that.
sentences.zh: 美国的出生率，我想很多人也是这样。

sentences.en: But what you seem to be describing is that those issues we do think about often, things like immigration and healthcare and climate change, that all of those are actually a part
sentences.zh: 但你所描述的似乎是，那些我们经常思考的问题，比如移民、医疗保健和气候变化，其实所有这些都是这个增长率问题的一部分，

sentences.en: of this growth rate question and that doing something about the birth rate will require thinking about all of these issues all at once?
sentences.zh: 而要对出生率采取行动，就需要同时思考所有这些问题？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right,
sentences.zh: 是的，没错，

sentences.en: Isted.
sentences.zh: 埃斯特德。

sentences.en: I mean, it seems like just a nerdy little number, but the truth is it's incredibly important because it touches on almost every aspect of American life.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来像是一个书呆子气的小数字，但事实是它极其重要，因为它触及了美国生活的几乎方方面面。

sentences.en: I mean, think about it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，想想看。

sentences.en: Immigration, the social safety net, health insurance, hospitals,
sentences.zh: 移民、社会安全网、健康保险、医院、

sentences.en: elder care, the role of government, how large it should be.
sentences.zh: 老人护理、政府的角色以及它应该有多大。

sentences.en: I mean, these are huge arguments in this country and they have been for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些都是这个国家长期以来争论不休的重大问题。

sentences.en: And the problem is we as Americans have gotten unused to thinking of ourselves as one group.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，我们作为美国人已经习惯了不把自己当成一个整体来思考。

sentences.en: It's much less we and much more I.
sentences.zh: 我们很少说“我们”，更多的是说“我”。

sentences.en: We've become tribal in a way that will really complicate collective decision-making on these really, really important issues.
sentences.zh: 我们在某种程度上变得部落化了，这会让在这些非常非常重要的问题上进行集体决策变得极其复杂。

sentences.en: So that is potentially a very serious problem because we are barreling toward a very fundamental change in American society.
sentences.zh: 因此，这可能是一个非常严重的问题，因为我们正全速冲向美国社会的一个根本性变革。

sentences.en: And it is going to take all of our collective effort to solve this problem.
sentences.zh: 解决这个问题需要我们付出全部的集体努力。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for your time.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: Thank you, Ested.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，埃斯特德。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费探索《时报》一个月，甚至不需要输入信用卡，会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载

sentences.en: The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅者，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，并获得 30 天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: The Times reports that the FDA is preparing to authorize the use of
sentences.zh: 据《时报》报道，美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）正准备在

sentences.en: Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine in adolescents
sentences.zh: 下周初之前批准辉瑞新冠疫苗在

sentences.en: 12 to 15 years old by early next week.
sentences.zh: 12至15岁青少年中的使用授权。

sentences.en: That would mark a crucial new phase in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这将标志着美国

sentences.en: vaccination campaign since immunizing children is considered essential to limiting the spread of the virus.
sentences.zh: 疫苗接种运动的关键新阶段，因为让儿童免疫被认为是限制病毒传播的关键。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 还有……

sentences.en: Today is a milestone for New York State and a significant moment of transition.
sentences.zh: 今天是纽约州的一个里程碑，也是一个重要的过渡时刻。

sentences.en: On Monday, officials from three neighboring states,
sentences.zh: 周一，来自三个相邻州的官员——

sentences.en: New York,
sentences.zh: 纽约州、

sentences.en: New Jersey, and Connecticut, said they would allow many businesses to fully reopen on May 19th, from restaurants and offices to theaters and gyms and said they were acting together
sentences.zh: 新泽西州和康涅狄格州表示，他们将允许许多企业在 5 月 19 日全面重新开放，从餐馆、办公室到剧院和健身房，并表示他们采取共同行动是因为他们的经济深度互联。

sentences.en: because their economies are deeply interconnected.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个三州地区。

sentences.en: We live in a tri-state area.
sentences.zh: 我们说康涅狄格州的餐馆开门了，但纽约没有。

sentences.en: We say the restaurants are open in Connecticut, but not in New York.
sentences.zh: 你就会看到纽约人开车去康涅狄格州。

sentences.en: You'll have New Yorkers driving to Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 你就会看到纽约人开车去新泽西州。

sentences.en: You'll have New Yorkers driving to New Jersey.
sentences.zh: （原文缺失/句尾结束标志）

sentences.en: The coordination is important.
sentences.zh: 这种协调至关重要。

sentences.en: But there were caveats.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些附加条件。

sentences.en: In New York, for instance, businesses will still have to abide by the federal government's six-foot social distancing rules unless they require workers and customers
sentences.zh: 例如在纽约，企业仍需遵守联邦政府关于六英尺社交距离的规定，除非它们要求工人和顾客

sentences.en: to provide proof that they are vaccinated or that they have tested negative for the virus.
sentences.zh: 提供已接种疫苗或病毒检测呈阴性的证明。

sentences.en: Finally,
sentences.zh: 最后，

sentences.en: President Biden said he would allow about 62,000 refugees into the U.S.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统表示，他将在未来六个月内

sentences.en: over the next six months, reversing a limit of 15,000 put in place by President Trump.
sentences.zh: 允许大约62,000名难民进入美国，从而推翻了特朗普总统设定的一万五千人的限制。

sentences.en: A few weeks ago,
sentences.zh: 几周前，

sentences.en: Biden had said he would maintain the 15,000 limit, drawing criticism from Democratic lawmakers and advocates for refugees and prompting the White House to change course.
sentences.zh: 拜登曾表示他将维持一万五千人的限制，这招致了民主党议员和难民倡导者的批评，并促使白宫改变了立场。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Luke Vanderplug and Eric Krupke.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由卢克·范德普勒格和埃里克·克鲁普克制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Paige Cowett and engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由佩奇·考维特剪辑，克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on
sentences.zh: 本周在

sentences.en: The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 《Wirecutter秀》节目中，我们将为节日期间的招待做好准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人们宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们对光线敏感吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝到断片才睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线环境，因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏史或食物不耐受吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们习惯喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序上或在你喜欢的任何播客平台上搜索《Wirecutter秀》。
